nodes.label: R11 Terminal Condition: GOVERNED HOLD — HUMAN DECISION REQUIRED
nodes.rationale: The hold is genuine because machine-resolvable work is exhausted, but the basis changed: the approval ledger reconciles (27 - 15 = 12) so there is no lifecycle bug; `standard` is project-explicit; the 14 'Ready with Warnings' are withdrawn as progress because they rest on a fail-open safety gate; the non-product commercial gap is an architectural defect requiring an atomic schema slice, not data entry.

nodes.label: Approval Ledger Reconciliation (31 events / 27 unique / 15 invalidated / 12 current)
nodes.rationale: The prior '22 system approvals' was an undercount of its own actions. `estimator_understanding_review_events` is the authoritative audit table; `confirmedSpecifications()` feeds Confirmed requirement links into the Understanding input fingerprint, so creating 68 Confirmed links shifted the fingerprint and invalidated 15 approvals. `safeUnderstandingReviewItem` downgrading a non-matching approval is correct fail-safe governance, not a lifecycle bug.

nodes.label: CRITICAL DEFECT: Panel-Compatibility Gate Fails Open
nodes.rationale: `executeRequirementProfile` builds profile identity as `approvedProductFamily || item.subcategory || item.category`, so with no approved Understanding the raw BOQ-extractor noun ('Detector', 'Module', 'Control Panel') becomes classification authority. `fireAlarmCategoryForFamily` returns null for those nouns, so `fireAlarmRequiresPanelCompatibility` returned false and a safety-relevant gate silently switched off. The system records provenance 'BOQ Extraction' — it knows the value is unapproved — and still lets it disable a governed safety gate. Not repaired in this mission because repair changes cross-project readiness policy.

nodes.label: Lump Sum / Non-Product Commercial Path Defect
nodes.rationale: 12 rows (17 in the engineering denominator) are `unit = Lump Sum` interface/integration obligations with no device identity, so `quotation-line-authority` marks the whole project not ready and `cost-buildup-model` COST_READY requires material cost. The conflation is emergent, not encoded: `product_id`/`candidate_id` are NOT NULL with no `line_type` discriminator. The fail-closed behaviour is correct — rows are retained and truthfully block rather than being silently dropped — but repair needs an atomic 4-part slice plus a new migration. Guardrail: `NO_PRODUCT_FAMILY`/`DATA_QUALITY_EXCLUDED` must not be used as the qualifying predicate because a door contact also carries NO_PRODUCT_FAMILY.

nodes.label: `standard` Resolved by Project Evidence (PROJECT EXPLICIT)
nodes.rationale: The Al Mousa specification names the standards verbatim, and `spec-source-fact-promotion.mjs` already promoted family-scoped `applicable_standard` facts consumed by `technical-requirement-engine.mjs` `sourceFactStandards`, which satisfies the `standard` gate with no requirement link. Escalating `standard` to a human was premature; what remains is verification of a deterministic extraction, not an engineering judgment. The 12-gate auto-confirm policy yields 0 eligible of 457, and the standards glossary rows are correctly Informational — so the mandatory 'Comply with UL 521'-style clauses are the right source, not the glossary.

nodes.label: `compatibilityTarget` Unsatisfiable Pre-Selection (Intentional Governance)
nodes.rationale: The project mandates a single-manufacturer UL-listed ecosystem and an approved-vendor list (Simplex / Honeywell / Siemens) — a constraint, not a named panel. `technical-requirement-engine.mjs:300-306` deliberately adds `protocol_compatibility` facts to compatibility evidence while carrying neither `targetItem` nor `rightEntityId`, because the gate requires a named compatible PRODUCT/PANEL. Sprint 1.14 made the gate family-conditional. So the field cannot logically exist before panel selection, and asking a human to 'fill the field' now is the wrong question.

nodes.label: Partial Fact-Level Authority Gap in Understanding
nodes.rationale: `estimator_understanding_review_items` is one row, one status, one opaque `canonical_interpretation` blob; origins are only EXTRACTED|INFERRED|MISSING|NOT_APPLICABLE with no CONFIRMED origin, so no per-field state is representable. Four working precedents exist one layer down (classification decisions, intelligence facts, profile applicability, drawing title-block field reviews). The all-or-nothing auto-approval policy is intentional and test-pinned and must NOT be weakened — the real symptom is the absence of anywhere to record a partial verdict.

nodes.label: EDIT_AND_APPROVE Interim Path (family confirmed, attributes unresolved)
nodes.rationale: Available today without structural change: a human can approve the classification while setting unsupported attributes to MISSING as one human action. This is the correct interim path for the 12 items whose family is deterministic but whose proposal is too rich, and it requires no code change.

nodes.label: Candidate-Generation / Selection / Engineering-Approval Boundary
nodes.rationale: product-matching-api gates matching on `understandingAttempt.available` only — not on `readiness_status` or `approved_for_matching` — and only APPROVED canonical facts feed classification search. `approved_for_matching` is read solely by dashboard and excel-export. The authority boundary is correctly drawn and must be preserved; the defect is upstream, in classification provenance.

nodes.label: Classification-Required Root-Cause Groups (No interpretation / B / C / E / F)
Eight Genuine Human Decisions (evidence-backed packet)
nodes.rationale: Machine-resolvable questions are explicitly EXCLUDED from the packet: 'Confirm Smoke Detector is a Smoke Detector', 'Confirm the standard per item', or any re-typing of a deterministically derived value.

nodes.label: Ready-with-Warnings Gate Assessment (`approve-readiness`)
nodes.rationale: `approve-readiness` sets `approved_for_matching=1`, which is genuinely a technical decision that the item's requirement set is a safe basis for product search — not a workflow acknowledgement. All 14 warnings are non-blocking only because of the panel-compatibility fail-open defect.
